title: Cosmic Lighthouses
narration: Everything dies, but this star screams hundreds of times a second for billions of years. A pulsar: a neutron star, ten kilometers across, spinning up to seven hundred sixteen times per second.
visual_goal: Dark space, a bright beam sweeping from a distant star, rhythmic light pulses.

title: Chance Discovery
narration: In nineteen sixty-seven, Jocelyn Bell Burnell spotted a signal blinking with remarkable regularity. The chart anomaly was dismissed as a bit of scruff, but the signal, nicknamed LGM-one for Little Green Men, was the first pulsar, a cosmic lighthouse sweeping its beam across Earth.
visual_goal: 1960s radio telescope, pen tracing spikes on paper, surprised woman scientist.

title: Extreme Physics
narration: These stars are ten kilometers across yet pack one point four solar masses. Gravity crushes matter denser than an atomic nucleus—a teaspoon would punch through Earth. It spins faster than a dentist's drill.
visual_goal: Tiny star vs. sun, then fast-spinning small star with jets.

title: Precision Tools
narration: Perfect pulsar timing catches a thief—even a planet. In nineteen ninety-two, variations revealed the first exoplanets. By two thousand twenty-three, sixty-eight pulsars detected a gravitational wave background—ripples in spacetime.
visual_goal: Pulsar with planets, then spacetime grid with gravitational waves.

title: Eternal Signals
narration: Each pulse echoes a star's death. They slow down, reminding us the universe's most precise clocks are winding down. Their timing gave us planets, gravity waves, and a new way to hear the cosmos. We are listening.
visual_goal: Pulsar signals reaching Earth, radio dish listening, starfield fading to black.
